name: Held By Human
description: An account in some system belongs to this person: an Okta user, a Duo user, a Teleport user or a GitLab user is held by one human. The source is WILDCARD (omitted), like TRUSTS_ISSUER, so any vendor's account type can point here without identity_core depending upward on the vendor plugin. Wildcard means the schema accepts ANY entity type as the source, not only accounts: nothing here can tell an account type from any other, so 'the source is an account' is kept by whoever draws the edge, and a traversal that needs accounts only should filter the source type. The edge is an assertion that two records are the same person; it is drawn by whoever knows that (an operator's seed, an HR feed, a collector matching an immutable identifier) and never inferred from a shared display name or email address. An account held by nobody has no edge; that is the unmatched state an access review must show, not an error. Cardinality is not constrained: an account may point at more than one human. That is a shared account (a break-glass login, a team mailbox, a service account several people know the password to), and an access review must be able to see it, so the edge records it instead of refusing it.

matched_on.description: How the account was tied to the person, in one phrase (for example "operator seed", "HR employee id", "Okta immutable id"). Blank means not recorded, not unmatched.
